title: Next launch for The Connection Code: women's relationship problems

ideas.buyer: Married women (25-45) who have just found chats, photos or proof that their husband is cheating
ideas.title: I Found The Chats: What To Do After You Discover He's Cheating
ideas.problem: She has just seen the messages. She can't tell her family (they'll say 'all men cheat, endure'), she can't tell her friends, and she doesn't know whether to confront, stay, leave, or protect her health first.

score_notes.P: Same cry for help recurring on Nairaland across ~15 years of thread IDs (659353 to 8094593), incl. 'I Caught My Husband ... Pls Advise Me!' and 'How Do I Cope With Cheating Husband?'
score_notes.W: Women already pay N5,000-50,000 per counselling session; PIs and spiritual 'remedies' are also bought. Named price exists, but no direct ebook traction observed, so 4 not 5
score_notes.G: Affair-recovery reading lists are all US/Canadian authors (Glass, Spring, Snyder/Baucom); local advice in circulation is documented as harmful ('ashawo vibes', 'a cheating husband is better than a dead one', 'confess righteousness out of him')

ideas.substitute: Marriage counselling N5,000-50,000/session (Nigeria); private investigators; pastors; traditional/spiritual 'remedies'
ideas.existing: US affair-recovery books (Glass, Spring, Snyder et al.); a Selar novel about a cheating husband (fiction, not help); generic 'Husband Manual' Selar ebook
ideas.gap: Nobody gives a Nigerian wife a calm, step-by-step plan for the first 72 hours and 30 days after discovery: protect her health and money, what to say when she confronts him, how to answer family who tell her to endure, and how to decide stay or leave on her own terms.
contents: The first 72 hours: what to do before you say a word
Protect yourself first: health test, money, documents
Confronting him: the exact words, and what his reaction tells you
'All men cheat': answering family, in-laws and the pastor
Stay or leave: a decision you make, not one made for you
If you stay: the conditions that make rebuilding possible
If you leave: the practical first steps
Safety and help: when it is more than cheating
ideas.hook: You found the chats. Before you confront him, read this.
ideas.channel: Facebook (marriage groups + Meta ads, women 25-45) -> WhatsApp -> Selar
ideas.watch_out: Must never counsel staying in abuse; include STI-testing advice framed medically-neutral, abuse/helpline pointers, and no 'get him back' manipulation tactics. Ad copy must not assert the viewer's situation ('Your husband is cheating') - use scene-based hooks.

ideas.buyer: Wives whose husband takes his mother's side or whose in-laws interfere

score_notes.P: Nairaland recurrence from thread 9548 ('How Long Can Your Mother-In-Law Stay With You?') to 7575793, plus a large Quora cluster of near-identical questions
score_notes.W: No in-law-specific price found; only general counselling spend. Capped at 3
score_notes.G: Free advice is principle-only ('better to lose an argument than the relationship'); gap for scripts inferred, so capped at 3

ideas.substitute: General marriage counselling; pastors; family mediation
ideas.existing: Free forum and Quora advice; Western in-law books (not checked this run)
ideas.gap: Word-for-word scripts for getting a Nigerian husband to set the boundary himself, without the wife being cast as the villain.

market_notes: Acute-crisis problems (just found out) convert better on cold ads than chronic ones (still waiting), because the buyer wants help tonight.
Price the first product at N2,500-3,000 with a $6-7 diaspora price; N4,500 for an unknown brand stalled.
Meta ads must not assert the viewer's personal situation; use scene-based hooks.
